topic: VPN client shows a connection timeout
title: VPN client connection timeout – cannot reach gateway
symptoms: VPN client shows "Connection timed out" error
Cannot access internal resources
Internet browsing works but VPN fails
Client status shows disconnected
cause: The client cannot reach the VPN gateway, usually because the local internet connection is down, the gateway is unreachable, or the client software is corrupted.
resolution_steps: Verify internet connectivity by opening a public website
Confirm the VPN server address in the client settings is correct
Close and restart the VPN client application
Reboot the computer to clear any residual network state
If the problem remains, uninstall the VPN client and reinstall the latest version from the company software portal
After reinstall, launch the client and attempt to connect using your credentials
escalate_if: If the issue persists after reinstall, if a different error code appears, or if multiple users in the same location experience the same timeout, contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: VPN connects but internal sites do not load
title: VPN connects but internal sites fail to load
symptoms: VPN client shows a connected status
Intranet web pages do not load
Browser shows DNS or timeout errors
Network drives are inaccessible
cause: The most common cause is that DNS settings or routing tables are not updated after the VPN connection, often due to a stale network session or cached DNS entries.
resolution_steps: Confirm the corporate VPN client shows a green connected indicator
Open a command prompt and run ipconfig /flushdns
Run ipconfig /release and then ipconfig /renew to obtain a fresh address
Restart the corporate VPN client and reconnect
Verify that the DNS server list includes the corporate DNS servers
Attempt to reach an internal site by name and by IP address
If the problem persists, reboot the workstation
If after reboot the issue remains, open a ticket with the Service Desk
escalate_if: If internal sites are still unreachable after completing all steps, or if the VPN disconnects repeatedly, the employee should contact the Service Desk for deeper network analysis.

topic: VPN disconnects every few minutes
title: VPN connection drops every few minutes
symptoms: VPN disconnects after a short period
Internet access stops when VPN is active
Error message indicating lost tunnel
cause: The most common cause is an unstable network link, often due to weak Wi‑Fi signal, aggressive power‑saving settings, or frequent network switching.
resolution_steps: Verify that the Wi‑Fi signal strength is strong; move closer to the access point or switch to a wired Ethernet connection
Disable any power‑saving options for the wireless adapter in the operating system settings
Make sure the corporate VPN client is set to use the default network adapter and not a specific one that may be turned off
Restart the VPN client and reconnect to the corporate VPN
Check for and install the latest VPN client update from the company software portal
If using a laptop, ensure the device is plugged in or set to ‘High performance’ power mode
Confirm that no other VPN or proxy software is running simultaneously
Test the connection on a different network (e.g., mobile hotspot) to rule out local network issues
escalate_if: If the disconnects continue after completing all steps, or if the employee experiences frequent disconnections on multiple networks, they should contact the Service Desk for deeper investigation and possible server‑side troubleshooting.

topic: Wi-Fi keeps dropping in the office
title: Office Wi‑Fi connection drops intermittently
symptoms: Frequent loss of wireless connectivity
Network icon shows disconnected
Web pages fail to load
Need to reconnect to Wi‑Fi repeatedly
cause: The typical cause is a weak or unstable wireless signal combined with outdated network adapter drivers on the device.
resolution_steps: Verify you are within range of an access point and move closer if possible
Forget the corporate Wi‑Fi network on the device and reconnect using the company software portal credentials
Update the wireless network adapter driver to the latest version from the vendor or via the corporate software portal
Disable and re‑enable the Wi‑Fi adapter in the device’s network settings
Restart the device to apply changes
If the issue persists, check for interference from other electronics and note this for escalation
escalate_if: Contact the Service Desk if the Wi‑Fi drops continue after driver update and reconnection, or if multiple users in the same area experience the same problem

topic: Internet is very slow on the office network
title: Internet speed is slow on office network
symptoms: Web pages load slowly
Speed test shows low throughput
Video streaming buffers frequently
File downloads take longer than usual
cause: Usually the slowdown is due to network congestion, bandwidth‑heavy applications, or a suboptimal wired/wireless connection.
resolution_steps: Run a speed test from a wired connection to establish a baseline
Close any bandwidth‑heavy applications such as large file transfers, streaming services, or cloud sync clients
Verify you are using an Ethernet connection; if on Wi‑Fi, move closer to the access point or switch to wired
Restart the corporate VPN client to ensure optimal routing
Inspect the network cable and port for damage, reseat the connector or try a different port
Clear the browser cache and disable unnecessary extensions
If the issue persists, run a ping test to the corporate gateway and record latency
escalate_if: If the speed remains below 20 Mbps, latency exceeds 150 ms, or multiple users report the same slowdown after completing the steps, contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: One website will not open while others work
title: Single website fails to load while others work
symptoms: The specific site does not load or shows a 'Server not found' error
All other websites load normally in the same browser
Page load times out after several seconds
cause: The most common cause is a stale or corrupted DNS cache on the workstation, sometimes combined with a browser cache issue or temporary site outage.
resolution_steps: Close all browser windows and reopen the browser
Clear the browser cache for the affected site or use an incognito/private window
Flush the local DNS cache (e.g., run ipconfig /flushdns on Windows or dscacheutil -flushcache on macOS)
Try accessing the site using a different browser to rule out browser‑specific problems
Check the site status using an external service or a colleague’s computer to confirm the site is up
If a proxy or firewall is configured, verify that the site is not blocked and temporarily disable the proxy to test
Restart the network adapter or reboot the computer if the problem persists
escalate_if: If the site still does not load after completing all steps, or if the DNS flush reports errors, contact the Service Desk for further network diagnostics or possible firewall rule adjustments

topic: VPN rejects the login or never asks for the MFA code
title: VPN login fails or does not prompt for MFA
symptoms: VPN client disconnects immediately after entering credentials
No MFA prompt appears
Error message indicates authentication failure
Repeated login attempts lock the account
cause: The most common cause is a mismatch between the device’s time and the authentication server, or an outdated or unregistered authenticator app, which prevents the MFA challenge from being generated.
resolution_steps: Verify the device clock is set to automatic time and the correct time zone
Ensure the device has an active internet connection
Open the corporate VPN client and disconnect any existing sessions
Re‑register the authenticator app via the company software portal
Clear saved credentials in the VPN client and re‑enter username and password
Attempt to connect again and respond to the MFA prompt
If the problem persists, reset any account lock via the self‑service portal or contact the Service Desk
escalate_if: If the login still fails after re‑registering the authenticator and confirming time sync, or the account remains locked, the employee should contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: Laptop cannot join the corporate Wi-Fi network
title: Laptop unable to connect to corporate Wi-Fi network
symptoms: Unable to see the corporate SSID
Connection attempt fails with authentication error
Frequent disconnections after login
Cannot access internal resources after connecting
cause: The most common cause is an outdated Wi‑Fi credential cache or an expired corporate authentication certificate stored on the laptop.
resolution_steps: Open the Wi‑Fi settings, locate the corporate network and select the option to forget or remove the network profile
Restart the laptop to clear any cached network data
Access the company software portal and download the latest corporate Wi‑Fi authentication certificate
Install the downloaded certificate using the on‑screen prompts
Re‑join the corporate Wi‑Fi network and re‑enter your username and password
Test the connection by opening an internal web page or pinging a known internal server
escalate_if: If the laptop still cannot obtain an IP address or authentication continues to fail after completing the steps, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: How to request access to a project tool such as Jira
title: Request Access to Project Management Tool (e.g., Jira)
symptoms: Cannot view project board
Receiving permission error when trying to create tickets
User not listed in the project tool
cause: The employee lacks the necessary permissions because an access request has not been submitted or approved.
resolution_steps: Confirm which project tool and specific project(s) you need access to
Obtain written approval from your manager (email or document)
Log in to the company software portal and locate the access request form
Enter your name, employee ID, manager name, tool name, and a brief justification for access
Attach the manager approval document to the form
Submit the request and note the reference number provided
Wait for the automated confirmation email and approval notification (typically 1‑3 business days)
Log in to the tool to verify access; if access is still missing, proceed to escalation
escalate_if: If access is not granted within three business days after manager approval or you receive a rejection notice, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: Install approved software from the company software portal
title: How to Install Approved Software from the Company Software Portal
symptoms: Required application is missing from the workstation
Unable to locate the software in the start menu
Installation prompts do not appear when trying to run the installer
cause: The employee has not used the self‑service portal to request the approved application, or the installation request was not initiated correctly. In some cases the portal may be inaccessible due to network issues.
resolution_steps: Log onto the corporate network using the corporate VPN client if you are working remotely
Open a web browser and navigate to the company software portal
Sign in with your corporate username and password
Search for or browse to the desired approved application
Select the application and click the Install button, then wait for the progress indicator to finish
When the installation completes, verify the program appears in the start menu or program list
escalate_if: If the installation fails, displays an error code, or the application does not appear after the process completes, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: An application crashes when it starts
title: Application crashes immediately after launch
symptoms: The program closes as soon as it opens
Error dialog appears with code 0x8000xxxx
No response after splash screen
Performance slows before crash
cause: The most common cause is corrupted local files or a stale cache that prevents the application from loading correctly.
resolution_steps: Restart the computer to clear any temporary processes.
Verify that the corporate VPN client is connected if the application requires network access.
Delete the application’s cache folder located in the user profile directory.
Run a repair installation from the company software portal.
If the repair does not resolve the issue, uninstall the application and reinstall it using the latest package from the portal.
Confirm that the operating system has all recent updates installed.
escalate_if: If the application still crashes after completing all steps, contact the Service Desk and provide the error details; escalations are required when the issue persists on multiple devices or after a fresh reinstall.

topic: Software license has expired or will not activate
title: Software License Expired or Activation Failed
symptoms: License warning pop‑up appears
Application refuses to start
Feature access is blocked
Error message indicates license not valid
cause: The license assigned to the user has reached its expiration date or was never properly assigned in the licensing system.
resolution_steps: Close the affected application
Sign out of the corporate VPN client and sign back in to refresh credentials
Open the company software portal and go to the license management page
Verify that a valid license is listed under your user account
If no license or it is expired, submit a license renewal request through the portal
After renewal, sign out of the application and sign back in to trigger activation
If activation still fails, clear the application's local license cache by deleting the license file in your user profile
Restart the application and confirm the license is active
escalate_if: If the license remains expired after renewal or you cannot locate a license assignment, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: Internal web application will not load in the browser
title: Internal web application fails to load – blank page or certificate warning
symptoms: Blank page displayed after navigating to the app
Browser shows a security certificate warning
Page loads slowly and never completes
cause: Usually caused by an expired or untrusted SSL certificate, corrupted browser cache, or loss of VPN connectivity to the corporate network.
resolution_steps: Verify you are connected to the corporate VPN client
Ensure the URL is correct and uses https
Clear the browser cache and cookies for the site
Open the site in a private/incognito window
Try a different supported browser
If a certificate warning appears, view the certificate details and confirm it is issued by the corporate CA; if trusted, accept it
escalate_if: If the page still shows a blank screen or certificate warning after completing the steps, or if the VPN connection cannot be established, contact the Service Desk

topic: Access denied to a shared network folder
title: Access Denied to Shared Network Folder – Permission Error
symptoms: Error message indicates access is denied
Unable to open files in the folder
Folder appears with a red X icon
Credential prompt repeats when trying to open
cause: The user lacks the required NTFS or share permissions for the folder, or the network path entered is incorrect. This results in a permission error when the system attempts to grant access.
resolution_steps: Confirm the network path is correct and you are connected to the corporate network or VPN
Refresh the folder view or disconnect and reconnect to the shared drive
Verify you are logged in with the correct domain account; log off and log back in if needed
Test access to the same folder from another computer to rule out a local issue
If the path and account are correct, request read/write permission from the folder owner or your manager
After permission is granted, disconnect and reconnect to the share to apply the new rights
escalate_if: If the folder remains inaccessible after verifying the path and requesting permission, or if a different error code appears, contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: Cannot sign in to the single sign-on portal
title: Unable to Sign In to the Single Sign‑On Portal
symptoms: Login page reloads repeatedly
Error message about authentication failure
MFA prompt never appears
Access denied after entering credentials
cause: The most common cause is corrupted browser session data or an out‑of‑date authentication token, often combined with an incorrect password or mismatched MFA configuration.
resolution_steps: Close all browser windows and clear cookies and site data for the SSO domain
Open a new private/incognito browsing window
Navigate to the corporate SSO portal URL
Enter your username and password, confirming they are correct
Complete the multi‑factor authentication prompt
If the login loop continues, try a different supported browser or update the current browser to the latest version
Verify the device’s date, time, and time zone are correct
If the issue persists, reset your password via the password self‑service portal
escalate_if: If after completing all steps the employee still cannot access the portal, or receives an account lockout or MFA configuration error, they should contact the Service Desk; the ticket should be escalated to the Identity Management team if the problem appears to be a backend authentication service outage.

topic: Application update fails or is stuck installing
title: Application Update Fails or Remains Stuck During Installation
symptoms: Update progress bar does not move
Error message appears indicating failure
Installation window remains open without completing
cause: The update usually cannot finish because required disk space is insufficient, background processes lock files, or corrupted temporary files interfere with the installer.
resolution_steps: Close the application and any related programs
Ensure at least 500 MB of free disk space on the drive where the app is installed
Restart the computer to clear locked files
Open the corporate VPN client if working remotely, then launch the company software portal and start the update again
If the update still does not progress, delete the application’s temporary update folder (for example, %TEMP%\AppUpdate) and run the installer from the portal
If necessary, uninstall the application via the standard uninstall process, reboot, and reinstall the latest version from the portal
escalate_if: If the update still fails after reinstalling or error codes continue to appear, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: Laptop will not turn on or does not charge
title: Laptop Won’t Power On or Charge
symptoms: Laptop does not power on when the power button is pressed
Battery indicator shows no charge
Power LED remains off
Charger light does not illuminate
cause: The most common cause is a failure in the power delivery path, such as a faulty charger, a disconnected power source, or a battery that is not receiving charge.
resolution_steps: Verify the wall outlet is working by plugging in another device
Confirm the charger is securely connected to both the laptop and the outlet
Inspect the charger cable and connector for visible damage
Disconnect the charger, then press and hold the power button for about 15 seconds to release residual power
Reconnect the charger and attempt to power on the laptop
If the laptop still does not turn on, try a known‑good charger compatible with the device
If the laptop has a removable battery, remove it, reinsert it, and repeat the power‑on attempt
escalate_if: If the laptop remains unresponsive after using a known‑good charger and completing all steps, or if the battery appears swollen or damaged, the employee should contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: Laptop is very slow or freezes
title: Laptop runs slowly or freezes during normal use
symptoms: System takes a long time to open applications
Frequent freezing or unresponsiveness
Slow file copying or saving
High CPU usage observed
cause: Typically caused by excessive background processes, insufficient free storage, or pending system updates that degrade performance.
resolution_steps: Save any work and perform a full restart of the laptop
Close unnecessary applications and background processes using the Task Manager
Check available disk space and free up at least 15% of the primary drive
Run the Disk Cleanup utility to remove temporary files
Use the company software portal to check for and install pending Windows updates
Disconnect the corporate VPN client if it is not required for the current task
Run hardware diagnostics from the company software portal to verify RAM and drive health
If the issue persists, reboot into safe mode and repeat the above steps
escalate_if: If performance does not improve after completing all steps, or if hardware diagnostics report errors, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: External monitor is not detected
title: External monitor not detected on workstation
symptoms: No second screen appears
Desktop background remains on primary monitor only
Display settings show only one monitor
Monitor power indicator is on but no image
cause: Usually the issue is a loose or faulty video cable, incorrect input selection on the monitor, or the graphics driver not recognizing the display.
resolution_steps: Verify the monitor power is on and brightness is set appropriately
Check that the video cable (HDMI, DisplayPort, VGA, or USB‑C) is firmly connected to both the monitor and the computer; reseat both ends
Ensure the monitor input source matches the cable type (e.g., select HDMI on the monitor’s on‑screen menu)
Open the display settings on the computer (right‑click desktop → Display settings) and click “Detect” to force a scan for additional displays
If the monitor is still not detected, restart the computer while the monitor remains connected
Update or reinstall the graphics driver from the company software portal if the driver is outdated or corrupted
Test the monitor with a different cable or connect a different monitor to the same port to isolate hardware failure
escalate_if: If after completing the steps the monitor still does not appear in display settings, or the cable and port have been tested with another monitor and still fail, the employee should contact the Service Desk for hardware replacement or further investigation

topic: Printer shows offline
title: Printer Shows Offline – Troubleshooting Guide
symptoms: Printer status shows offline in Windows
Print jobs stay in the queue and never print
Unable to connect to the printer from any workstation
Printer control panel shows no error lights
cause: The printer is typically offline because it has lost its network connection or the spooler on the workstation cannot communicate with the device. Power interruptions or changes to the network can also cause the printer to disappear from the list of available devices.
resolution_steps: Verify the printer is powered on and the power LED is lit
Confirm the printer and the workstation are connected to the same corporate network (wired or Wi‑Fi)
Power cycle the printer by turning it off, waiting 30 seconds, then turning it back on
On the workstation, open Devices and Printers (or the corporate printer management utility) and delete the offline printer entry
Add the printer again using its network address or by selecting it from the discovered devices list
Restart the print spooler service on the workstation (services.msc → Print Spooler → Restart)
Print a test page to confirm the printer is online
escalate_if: If the printer remains offline after completing all steps, or it does not appear in network scans, the employee should contact the Service Desk for further investigation and possible hardware replacement.

topic: Keyboard or mouse does not respond
title: Keyboard or Mouse Not Responding – Troubleshooting Guide
symptoms: No characters appear when typing
Cursor does not move
Device LEDs remain off
cause: Most often the issue is caused by depleted batteries in a wireless device, a loose or unplugged receiver, or a faulty USB connection.
resolution_steps: Verify the device is turned on and batteries are installed correctly
Replace the batteries with fresh ones if the device is wireless
Disconnect and reconnect the wireless receiver or USB plug, ensuring a firm connection
Plug the receiver or mouse/keyboard into a different USB port, preferably a USB 2.0 port
Restart the computer to allow the operating system to re‑detect the device
Open the device manager (or system settings) and confirm the input device is listed and enabled; if it shows an error, uninstall and let the system reinstall the driver
escalate_if: If after completing the steps the keyboard or mouse still does not work, or the device is not recognized in device manager, contact the Service Desk for further diagnostics or hardware replacement

topic: No sound or microphone not working in meetings
title: No Sound or Microphone Not Working During Meetings
symptoms: No audio comes out of speakers or headphones
Microphone does not pick up voice
Participants cannot hear you in the meeting
Audio device shows as disconnected in the meeting app
cause: The most common cause is an incorrect or muted audio device selection, low volume settings, or privacy settings that block microphone access.
resolution_steps: Open the meeting application and go to the audio settings
Select the correct speaker and microphone from the device dropdown lists
Ensure the speaker and microphone volume sliders are turned up and not muted
Check the operating system privacy settings to confirm the meeting app has permission to use the microphone
If using a headset, verify it is securely plugged in or paired via Bluetooth and test it with a voice recorder
Restart the meeting application and, if needed, reboot the computer
escalate_if: If sound or microphone still does not work after completing all steps, contact the Service Desk for hardware inspection or driver reinstallation

topic: Docking station or USB devices are not recognised
title: Docking station or USB devices not recognized
symptoms: External monitor stays blank
Keyboard and mouse do not respond
USB drive not listed in file explorer
Docking station LED does not turn on
cause: The most common cause is a loose or unpowered connection between the laptop and the docking station, or outdated docking station drivers.
resolution_steps: Verify the docking station is plugged into a working power outlet and the power LED is on
Disconnect and reseat the docking cable on both the dock and the laptop
Ensure all peripheral USB devices are firmly connected to the dock ports
Restart the laptop so it can re‑enumerate the dock hardware
Open the company software portal and install the latest docking station driver package
If the issue persists, test the laptop with a different dock or test the dock with another laptop to isolate the hardware
escalate_if: If after completing all steps the devices are still not recognized, or the dock shows no power indicator, contact the Service Desk

topic: Outlook keeps asking for a password
title: Outlook repeatedly prompts for password after closing and reopening
symptoms: Outlook repeatedly asks for email password
Credential prompt appears each time sending or receiving
Unable to send or receive messages without entering password
Saved credentials seem ignored
cause: The prompt is usually caused by corrupted or outdated cached credentials in the Windows Credential Manager or a damaged Outlook profile, which prevents the client from using stored authentication tokens.
resolution_steps: Close Outlook completely
Open Windows Credential Manager and delete any entries related to Office or Outlook
Restart the computer
Launch Outlook and, when prompted, enter the correct password and select the option to remember it
Verify that mail synchronizes without further prompts
If the issue persists, recreate the Outlook profile using the Mail setup in the Control Panel
Test sending and receiving email to confirm the problem is resolved
escalate_if: If the password prompt continues after clearing credentials and recreating the profile, or if the user receives an authentication error from the mail server, contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: Emails are stuck in the Outbox
title: Emails Stuck in Outbox – Troubleshooting Guide
symptoms: Messages remain in the Outbox and never send
No error message appears when sending
Send/receive button is active but no progress is shown
Large attachment appears to prevent sending
cause: The client is often set to Work Offline or an attachment exceeds the permitted size, causing the message to stay queued in the Outbox.
resolution_steps: Open the email client and verify that the Work Offline toggle is not enabled
If Work Offline is active, disable it to return to online mode
Check the size of any attachments; reduce or remove attachments larger than the company limit (e.g., 25 MB)
Close and restart the email client to clear any temporary cache
Navigate to the Outbox folder, select the stuck message, and click Send
If the message still does not leave the Outbox, delete it, recreate the email, and resend
Confirm network connectivity and that the mail server is reachable via the company software portal
escalate_if: If the email remains in the Outbox after completing all steps, or if error codes appear, the employee should contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: An email with a large attachment is rejected
title: Email with Large Attachment Rejected – How to Resolve
symptoms: Send operation fails with an error message
Attachment size exceeds the allowed limit warning
Recipient does not receive the email
Message remains in the outbox without being sent
cause: The corporate email system enforces a maximum attachment size (for example, 25 MB). When a file larger than this limit is attached, the server rejects the message during the send process.
resolution_steps: Check the size of the attachment using the file properties dialog
If the file is larger than the allowed limit, compress it into a ZIP archive or split it into smaller parts
If compression is insufficient, upload the file to the company software portal or shared drive and copy the generated shared link
Remove the original attachment from the email and insert the shared link in the message body
Resend the email and verify that it is delivered successfully
If the email is still rejected, confirm that the recipient’s mailbox does not have a lower attachment limit
If the problem persists after these steps, clear the email client cache or restart the client and try again
escalate_if: If the email still cannot be sent after compressing the file and using a shared link, or if the error message indicates a server‑side issue, the employee should contact the Service Desk for further investigation

topic: Meeting invites are missing or the calendar does not sync
title: Meeting invites missing or calendar not syncing
symptoms: Meeting invitations do not appear in the calendar
Existing events are not updating automatically
Calendar shows outdated or duplicate entries
Sync status indicator displays an error
cause: The issue is typically caused by a broken synchronization link between the email client and the calendar service, often due to network interruptions, an outdated client version, or a corrupted local cache.
resolution_steps: Verify that the device is connected to the corporate network or VPN and that internet access is functional
Open the email client and manually trigger a calendar refresh using the refresh or sync option
Check that the correct email account is selected for calendar sync in the client settings
Close the email client completely, then restart it to re‑initialize the sync process
If the problem persists, clear the client cache or temporary files via the client’s settings or reinstall the client from the company software portal
escalate_if: If calendar entries still do not appear after completing all steps, or the sync error persists for more than 30 minutes, contact the Service Desk for further investigation and possible server‑side troubleshooting

topic: Cannot sign in to the team chat app or messages will not send
title: Team Chat App Sign-In Failure or Unsent Messages
symptoms: Unable to sign in to the team chat app
Error message appears when attempting to log in
Messages do not deliver after being sent
Presence status shows as offline despite being online
cause: The issue is usually caused by a corrupted local cache, an expired authentication token, or a temporary outage of the chat service.
resolution_steps: Close the team chat app completely
Sign out from the app if still logged in
Clear the app’s cache and temporary files via system settings
Re‑launch the app and sign in again using corporate credentials
Verify internet connectivity and that the corporate VPN client is connected
Check the service status page on the company software portal for any ongoing incidents
If the problem persists, update the app to the latest version or reinstall it
escalate_if: If after completing the steps the user still cannot sign in or messages remain unsent, or if the service status shows an outage, the employee should contact the Service Desk

topic: How to set up an email signature and an out-of-office reply
title: Create Email Signature and Configure Out-of-Office Reply
symptoms: Outgoing emails have no signature
Recipients do not receive an automatic reply when I am away
Colleagues comment that my emails look incomplete
Automatic replies are not being sent despite being set
cause: The user has not set up a default signature or enabled the automatic reply feature in the corporate email client settings, so messages are sent without the expected branding and out-of-office notifications are not generated.
resolution_steps: Open the corporate email client and sign in with your corporate credentials
Select Settings, then choose Mail Settings
Navigate to the Signature section, click Add New, enter your name, title, phone number and any legal disclaimer, then save
Set the new signature as the default for new messages and replies
Return to Settings and select Automatic Replies (Out of Office)
Turn on automatic replies, specify the start and end dates, type the internal and external reply messages, and save the settings
escalate_if: If the signature still does not appear on sent messages or automatic replies are not sent after following the steps, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: A shared mailbox does not appear in Outlook
title: Shared mailbox not appearing in Outlook
symptoms: Shared mailbox is not listed in the folder pane
Cannot send email from the shared mailbox
Only personal mailbox folders are visible
cause: The user has recently been granted access but the permission changes have not yet propagated or Outlook cache has not refreshed.
resolution_steps: Confirm that Full Access or Send As permissions were granted for the shared mailbox
Allow up to 24 hours for permission replication
Close Outlook completely and restart the application
Manually add the shared mailbox: open Outlook account settings, choose the option to add additional mailbox, enter the shared mailbox name, and confirm
If the mailbox still does not appear, reset the Outlook navigation pane by running Outlook with the /resetnavpane switch
escalate_if: If the mailbox remains missing after the above steps or you encounter error messages while adding it, contact the Service Desk for further investigation.

topic: How to reset a forgotten password with self-service
title: Reset a Forgotten Password Using the Self-Service Portal
symptoms: Cannot log into corporate applications
Password entry is rejected
Account locked after multiple attempts
cause: The user’s password has expired or was forgotten, causing authentication failures.
resolution_steps: Open a web browser and navigate to the self-service password reset portal from the intranet
Enter your corporate username or email address and click Continue
Choose a verification method (mobile OTP, security questions, or email link) and complete the challenge
When identity is confirmed, enter a new password that meets complexity requirements and confirm it
Submit the change and note the confirmation message
Log in to the corporate VPN client or any application with the new password to verify it works
If any step fails, record the error message for escalation
escalate_if: If identity verification fails, you do not receive the reset email or OTP, or the portal returns an error after multiple attempts, contact the Service Desk

topic: Account is locked after too many failed sign-ins
title: Account Locked After Multiple Failed Sign‑In Attempts
symptoms: Sign‑in rejected with an account locked message
Unable to access corporate applications
Repeated login attempts produce the same error
Password prompt does not appear
cause: The corporate authentication system automatically locks the account after a predefined number of consecutive failed sign‑in attempts to protect against unauthorized access.
resolution_steps: Stop any further sign‑in attempts to avoid extending the lockout period
Wait for the automatic unlock window (usually 15 minutes)
If immediate access is required, open the company software portal and select the self‑service unlock option
Verify your identity using the provided method such as security questions or a verification code
Submit the unlock request and wait for confirmation
If the self‑service option is unavailable or the unlock fails, contact the Service Desk
Provide your username and any requested proof of identity to the Service Desk
The Service Desk will manually unlock the account and advise on a password reset if needed
escalate_if: Contact the Service Desk if the account remains locked after using self‑service unlock, if an error occurs during the unlock process, or if the lockout persists beyond the standard window. Escalate to the Identity Management team if the Service Desk cannot resolve the issue within 30 minutes.

topic: MFA code not received or a new phone needs to be set up
title: MFA code not received or need to set up a new phone
symptoms: No verification code arrives via SMS or authenticator app
Authentication prompt shows an error after code entry
The registered phone number displayed is incorrect
Time‑based code is rejected as invalid
cause: The most common reasons are an outdated or wrong phone number, the authenticator app’s clock being out of sync, or the device not being registered in the MFA system.
resolution_steps: Verify the phone number stored in the corporate VPN client or account settings and correct it if needed
Make sure the device can receive SMS messages and that carrier service is active
Open the authenticator app, go to settings and enable time sync or reinstall the app to reset the secret
If using a new phone, deregister the old device from the company software portal and enroll the new device following the on‑screen instructions
Generate a temporary code using backup codes or email verification if available
If the code still does not arrive, submit a request to the Service Desk to re‑register the device or reset MFA settings
escalate_if: Contact the Service Desk if no code is received after completing the above steps, if the employee cannot access backup codes, or if the MFA enrollment fails repeatedly

topic: Password has expired and cannot be changed
title: Password Expired – How to Reset It via the Company Software Portal
symptoms: Login attempts are rejected with a password‑expired message
Unable to access email or internal applications
Prompt to change password appears but the change fails
Corporate VPN client reports authentication failure
cause: The corporate password policy sets a maximum password age; once that limit is reached the system blocks authentication until the password is updated.
resolution_steps: Connect to the corporate network – use wired, Wi‑Fi, or the corporate VPN client if you are remote
Open a web browser and go to the company software portal
Log in with your username and the expired password; you will be redirected to the password‑change screen
Enter a new password that complies with the policy (minimum 12 characters, includes upper‑case, lower‑case, a number and a special character, and is not one of your last five passwords)
Confirm the new password and submit; wait for the success confirmation
Log out of the portal, then log back in with the new password to verify access
Update the saved password in email client, VPN client and any other services that use corporate credentials
escalate_if: If the password change returns an error, you remain unable to log in after three attempts, or the account becomes locked, contact the Service Desk for further assistance

topic: New employee: first login and account activation
title: First Login and Account Activation for New Employees
symptoms: Cannot log in with corporate credentials
Prompt to change temporary password appears
MFA enrollment screen is displayed
Security questions have not been set
cause: New employee accounts are provisioned with a temporary password and require an initial password change, multi‑factor authentication enrollment, and security question setup before full access is granted.
resolution_steps: Open the welcome email and note the temporary password and link to the company software portal
Navigate to the company software portal and sign in using your corporate username and the temporary password
When prompted, create a new permanent password that meets the complexity requirements
Enroll in multi‑factor authentication by selecting a method (authenticator app, text message, or hardware token) and completing the verification process
Answer the required security questions to finalize account recovery options
Log out of the portal then sign in again with your new password to confirm that the account is fully active
escalate_if: If the temporary password is rejected, the password change fails, MFA enrollment cannot be completed, or the account remains locked after these steps, contact the Service Desk for assistance

topic: Suspicious sign-in alert on my account
title: Suspicious sign‑in alert received on your corporate account
symptoms: Email notification about an unrecognized sign‑in
Pop‑up warning when logging into the corporate VPN client
Unable to access certain applications
Unexpected device listed in account security settings
cause: The alert is typically generated when the authentication system detects a sign‑in attempt from an unknown device, location, or IP address that does not match your normal usage patterns.
resolution_steps: Do not ignore the alert; open the notification to view sign‑in details
Compare the date, time, location and device information with your recent activity
If you recognize the sign‑in as legitimate, confirm it and consider adding the device to your trusted list
If you do not recognize the sign‑in, immediately change your password using the company software portal
After changing the password, enable multi‑factor authentication if it is not already active
Log out of all active sessions from the account security page
Remove any unfamiliar devices or sessions from the trusted devices list
Report the incident to the Service Desk and follow any additional instructions
escalate_if: If you did not initiate the sign‑in, if you cannot complete the password reset, or if the alert continues after following the steps, contact the Service Desk immediately and request escalation to the security team

topic: How to request administrator rights or elevated permissions
title: Requesting Administrator Rights or Elevated Permissions
symptoms: Unable to install required software
Access denied when modifying system settings
Cannot run scripts that need admin rights
cause: The corporate environment restricts admin privileges to protect security and stability. Elevated permissions are only granted after manager and IT approvals and are not assigned automatically.
resolution_steps: Identify the specific permission needed and the business justification for it
Obtain written approval from your manager for the requested access
Submit a ticket through the company software portal attaching the manager's approval and a brief justification
IT reviews the request, verifies approvals, and determines the appropriate access level
If approved, IT configures your account with the requested admin rights and notifies you
Test the new permissions to confirm they work for the intended task
escalate_if: If the ticket remains pending for more than two business days, the manager should follow up with the Service Desk, or if access is denied despite proper approvals, the employee should contact the Service Desk for escalation

topic: How to report a phishing email
title: How to Report a Phishing Email
symptoms: Unexpected sender requesting sensitive information
Email contains suspicious links or attachments
Urgent or threatening language urging immediate action
Spelling and grammar errors that seem unprofessional
cause: Phishing emails are crafted by malicious actors to trick recipients into revealing credentials, installing malware, or making unauthorized transactions.
resolution_steps: Do not click any links, open attachments, or reply to the message
Use the built‑in “Report Phishing” button in the corporate email client
If the button is unavailable, forward the entire email as an attachment to the security mailbox via the company software portal
Delete the phishing email from your inbox and then from the Deleted Items folder
If you clicked a link or entered credentials, change the affected password immediately and inform the Service Desk
escalate_if: Contact the Service Desk immediately if you have interacted with the email (clicked a link, opened an attachment, or entered credentials) or if the email appears to be a targeted spear‑phishing attempt.

topic: How to request new equipment or a replacement device
title: Requesting New or Replacement Equipment
symptoms: Current device is malfunctioning or broken
Need additional hardware for a project
Laptop battery no longer holds charge
Missing peripheral required for work
cause: The employee’s existing equipment is damaged, outdated, or insufficient for job requirements, prompting a need for new or replacement devices.
resolution_steps: Verify the specific equipment needed and confirm it is not already available within the department
Obtain written approval from your manager for the equipment request
Log in to the company software portal and locate the equipment request form
Complete the form with details of the required device, justification, and manager approval
Submit the request to the Service Desk for processing
Monitor your email for an approval or clarification notice from the Service Desk
When approved, note the estimated delivery time and collection location provided
Collect the equipment from the designated location and confirm receipt in the portal
escalate_if: If you do not receive an approval or delivery estimate within five business days, or if the requested item is marked unavailable, contact the Service Desk for assistance or to have the ticket escalated to the provisioning team

topic: IT support hours and how to raise an urgent issue
title: IT Support Hours and How to Raise an Urgent Issue
symptoms: Cannot access corporate VPN during business hours
Critical system outage affecting multiple users
Time‑sensitive request not being addressed
Repeated login failures preventing work
cause: Support staff are available only during defined business hours, and urgent issues are those that halt essential business functions or pose a security risk.
resolution_steps: Verify the problem is occurring during the defined support hours
Search the company software portal knowledge base for a known solution
If unresolved, submit a ticket via the portal and select the ‘Urgent’ priority
Provide a clear description, impact level, and your contact details in the ticket
For problems outside support hours, call the after‑hours emergency line listed on the intranet
If the urgent ticket is not acknowledged within 30 minutes, call the Service Desk directly
escalate_if: Contact the Service Desk immediately if the issue prevents you from performing core job functions, involves a security breach, or is not acknowledged within 30 minutes of submitting an urgent ticket.
